source_caption:
When George Lucas returned to direct Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace, he initially decided to stick with practical effects for the Jedi Master Yoda, bringing back legendary puppeteer Frank Oz to perform the character. However, the new puppet designed for the film—intended to look slightly younger to reflect the prequel’s timeline—was widely criticized by fans upon release for looking jarringly different from the original trilogy version, with many pointing out its stiff movements and somewhat cross-eyed appearance. The dissatisfaction with the physical prop was so profound that Lucas ultimately decided to erase it from existence. Following the successful implementation of a fully CGI Yoda in the subsequent prequels, Industrial Light & Magic was tasked with retroactively animating a digital replacement for Episode I. For the 2011 Blu-ray release of the film, the controversial 1999 puppet was entirely scrubbed from the movie and replaced with a CGI model, making the original theatrical puppet a piece of lost media only visible on older VHS, LaserDisc, and original DVD copies.

Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace (1999), directed by George Lucas, starring Liam Neeson, Ewan McGregor, Natalie Portman, Jake Lloyd. Two Jedi Knights escape a hostile blockade to find allies and come across a young boy who may bring balance to the Force, but the long-dormant Sith resurface to claim their original glory.

source_details.synopsis: Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace is a 1999 American epic space opera film written and directed by George Lucas in his first directorial effort since the original Star Wars, released in 1977. Produced by Lucasfilm Ltd. and distributed by 20th Century Fox, it is the fourth film in the Star Wars film series, the first film of the prequel trilogy and the first chronological chapter of the "Skywalker Saga." The film stars Liam Neeson, Ewan McGregor, Natalie Portman, Jake Lloyd, Ahmed Best, Ian McDiarmid, Anthony Daniels, Kenny Baker, Pernilla August, and Frank Oz.
